texts.title: The Crown's Due
texts.body: What you owed the crown has not been forgotten. {sovereign.name} of {sovereign.house} has sent for the debt with the full apparatus of state behind the request — not a threat, because the crown does not threaten; a reminder, which is worse. There are three ways a house pays what it owes a throne, and the one it chooses is remembered longer than the debt.

choices.pay_in_coin: Pay in coin. It will hurt; it will be over.
choices.pay_in_service: Pay in service. A year at the crown's disposal — and standing afterward.
choices.defy_the_crown: Refuse. Let the court see what your house has become.

texts.title: The Thing From the Rock
texts.body: You had nearly forgotten it: the find from the worthless seam, logged and locked and set aside. A steward's report brings it back — readings that have changed, a seal that is warmer than it should be, a technician who will not go into the vault alone any more. Whatever the markets called exotic, it is not inert. It is waiting, and it would like to be understood.

choices.study_it: Give it the attention it has been waiting for. Learn what it is.
choices.sell_it: Sell it to someone who asks no questions. Let it be their problem.
choices.seal_it: Three locks and a false label. Forget it, deliberately.

texts.title: The Old Words
texts.body: Years ago, in the small hours at the academy, you and {comrade.name} of {comrade.house} swore the old words to each other. Now the oath has come due — one of you needs the other, at a cost, in a world that has made you both more careful than you were. Blood you are given. This you chose. The question is whether the choosing still holds.

choices.call_on_them: Call on the oath. Ask for what you need, and be answered.
choices.stand_for_them: Keep the oath for {comrade.name}'s sake, publicly and at cost.
choices.let_it_lapse: Let the words pass unkept. You were children when you said them.

texts.title: The Remnant
texts.body: The coalition that formed against you has broken, and {rival.name} of {rival.house}, who organised it, is left holding the pieces — fewer allies than last season, debts called in, a reputation for failure that the court can smell. A broken enemy is a decision waiting to be made.

choices.finish_them: Finish it. Peel away what is left and leave one bitter house.
choices.bring_them_in: Offer {rival.name} a place. Yesterday's organiser, today's client.
choices.let_them_scatter: Let the remnants drift. You have made your point.

texts.title: What the Quarrel Became
texts.body: There was a time when {friend.name} of {friend.house} would have seen you ruined and called it justice. That time passed — you saw to it that it passed — and what is left between you is something neither of you has named. Correct. Cordial. Careful. It could stay that. It could become more.

choices.deepen_it: Name it. Make the old enemy a sworn friend.
choices.keep_it_civil: Leave it as it is. Not every mended thing needs to be more.

texts.title: The Spoiled Kit, Remembered
texts.body: It comes back at odd moments — the cut straps, the vanished orders, the inspection you failed for something you did not do. The academy is years behind you, and the lesson is still deciding what shape to take in you.

choices.trust_no_one: Watch every locker, every ledger, every back. Learn it thoroughly.
choices.let_it_go: Set it down. It made you harder; that was enough.

texts.title: The Household
texts.body: The great game pauses, briefly, at your own door. {spouse.name} is there — has been there, through all of it — and the evening is, for once, unclaimed.

choices.tend_it: Spend the evening on the marriage and nothing else.
choices.neglect_it: Work through it. Again. The house needs the hours.

texts.title: The Breaking Point
texts.body: It has been building for years — every choice made against your nature, every oath kept at a cost, every quarrel carried — and now something in you has given way. The household has noticed. The court will, soon. What you do with the break decides what kind of person stands up afterward.

choices.gather_yourself: Put yourself back together, privately. Stronger along the crack.
choices.lash_out: Break outward. Let everyone nearby pay for the pressure.
choices.withdraw: Withdraw for a season. Let the house run itself, badly, and come back whole.

texts.title: Unfamiliar Sails
texts.body: They are in your sky. Not a raid — nothing so honest — but a fleet flying {intruder.house}'s colours, holding station over your own worlds as if the lanes belonged to it, close enough that the harbour towns can read the names on the hulls. {intruder.name} has sent no word. The absence of a message is the message. A house answers its own sky or it does not; the galaxy will remember which.

choices.muster: Crew every hull, man every battery, burn the harbour lights all night. Let them count.
choices.protest: Protest to every court that will listen. Make it cost them in reputation.
choices.let_them_pass: Do nothing. They will leave, and you will have lost nothing but face.

texts.title: The Review
texts.body: The house's ships lie at anchor — more than one now, enough to be called a fleet without irony. A fleet is a promise the house makes to its enemies and its friends alike, and promises want inspecting.

choices.inspect_it: Walk the decks yourself. Ask the questions a name is not supposed to ask.
choices.parade_it: Parade it past the capital in review order. Let the houses count.
